---
title: "Weekly learning journal"
subtitle: "One short entry a week, due Thursday night"
---

The journal is a record of what you tried. Each week you set out to learn
something with AI (see [Learn it with AI](learn-with-ai.qmd)), and the journal
is where you write down how it went. It takes about 30 minutes. It is marked
complete or incomplete, and it is what you bring to Friday's small group.

## Weeks 1 to 3: the entry

Answer four questions. A few sentences each is enough.

```
1. What I set out to learn
   The topic, and why it matters for my work or my specialty.

2. How I used AI to learn it
   Which tool, which prompts, what I asked it to do.
   What worked well enough that I would do it again?

3. What went wrong, and how I noticed
   Something vague, wrong, made up, or unhelpful, and what tipped me off.
   (If nothing went wrong, what did I do to be sure?)

4. One thing I checked
   One claim that mattered, the source I checked it against, and
   whether the AI had it right.
```

**Optional: share a resource.** If you found a paper, video, podcast, or tool
worth a classmate's time, add one or two, with a sentence on why. The best ones
go into the [starter resources](../appendix/resources.qmd) for future students.

## Week 4: what you will keep

No new topic. Write a short piece, roughly 300 to 500 words:

- the two or three ways of using AI you will keep using in residency, and why,
- one place you decided AI does not belong in your work, and why,
- what you would tell an incoming intern who is nervous about these tools.

Draw on your weeks 1 to 3 entries. Prepare a five-minute version for your
Friday small group on November 6. Slides optional.

## Submission

In Canvas, as a text entry under that week's module, by Thursday night:
October 15, 22, and 29, and November 5 for the week 4 piece.
Plain text is fine.

## Using AI to write the journal

You may use AI to help you think, organise, or tidy your writing. The
experiences and the judgments must be yours. One sentence at the end saying how
you used AI on the entry, if you did, is enough. That is the same disclosure
journals and residency programs now expect.
